name: Flavored waters
anchor: Per-form sovereign beverage cells in the as-consumed liquid basis (EU 2023/915 juice and rice-drink cells, Codex CXS 193 fruit juices, EU 2024/1987 beverage nickel, EU canned-beverage tin, Hong Kong Cap 132V's named carbonated, tea, coffee and wine beverage entries, and the US and Hong Kong packaged-drinking-water quality standards), with dry leaf, bean and powder commodities anchored separately in their own as-sold basis and never converted between the two
native_basis_label: ready-to-drink liquid, as consumed (wet weight, single strength); a concentrate or a powder-to-liquid product is assessed as reconstituted to single strength per the manufacturer's own directions, which is the basis EU 2023/915 and Codex CXS 193 write into their juice cells and Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 writes into its beverage entries
scope_note: Packaged still and sparkling waters carrying added flavour, essence or a trace of fruit essence, sold as water with flavour and containing no meaningful nutritive or functional load: no added sugar or sugar-substitute sweetener system beyond a trace, no electrolyte or stimulant formulation, no juice declared as an ingredient at a level that makes the product a juice drink. Products that carry a formulated load (sweetener, electrolyte, caffeine, botanical extract, protein, added juice) are NOT flavoured waters for this purpose and route to the sports and energy drink row or the soft-drink row, because the water-law anchor family used here rests on the product being water plus flavour. Plain bottled drinking water and natural mineral water route to Category 8 by the taxonomy boundary rule; a flavoured water with a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16. This row's anchor family is the PACKAGED-DRINKING-WATER food law (US 21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards and the Hong Kong Cap 132V bottled-or-packaged-drinking-waters schedule), not the public-water-system maximum contaminant levels. US EPA and Health Canada drinking-water MCLs are water-utility instruments that regulate a distribution system rather than a packaged food, they belong to Category 8, and they are deliberately outside this row's audit scope and candidate set; where one of them is stricter than the value adopted here (Health Canada total mercury at 1 ug/L, for example) that is disclosed rather than adopted, because a utility-facing MCL is not a maximum level for a packaged beverage.
basis_guard: as[ _]consumed|wet weight|reconstituted|ready.to.drink|product as placed on market|\bjuice\b|single-strength|bottled water|portion ordinarily consumed
basis_guard_note: This row publishes a ready-to-drink liquid ceiling, so every named anchor must itself be written in a wet as-consumed (or as-placed-on-market liquid, or packaged-drinking-water) basis. The guard refuses any dry-commodity as-sold cell, any feed-basis cell, any food-contact migration limit and any article-content limit, because applying a dry leaf, bean or powder maximum level to a brewed or reconstituted liquid would be exactly the basis conflation Method v2.0 forbids. No brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented in either direction. Within that, this row's anchors are all packaged-drinking-water quality standards in a per-litre aqueous basis, which converts to ug/kg at 1 mg/L = 1000 ug/kg for a beverage of unit density; the register already carries the converted values and no further treatment is applied.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact beverage form and analyte in the row's declared native basis, with disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination where a species is bounded or is a method artifact, and a control where no defensible sovereign number and no supportable near-neighbour exist. Never occurrence-derived. Ready-to-drink and dry-commodity bases are never mixed and no brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented.

Pb.basis: as consumed, packaged aqueous beverage (read across from the US bottled-water quality standard)
Pb.label: No credible sovereign has written a lead maximum level for flavoured water specifically. The nearest applicable sovereign value is the US 21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standard for lead (5 ug/kg), adopted by disclosed read-across; the Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged-drinking-water cell (10 ug/kg) is the looser sibling and is disclosed.
Pb.substantiation: A flavoured water is, compositionally, packaged drinking water plus a flavour dose, and it is sold and consumed as water; the packaged-water quality standard is therefore the nearest applicable sovereign cell in an identical aqueous as-consumed basis. The competing candidate was the Hong Kong carbonated-beverage lead cell (200 ug/kg), which does directly cover a sparkling flavoured water as a carbonated beverage. Both are applicable to forms in this row, so Method v2.0 step 3 compels the strictest applicable value, and that is 5 ug/kg, not 200. Adopting 200 here would have been the convenience choice and is expressly rejected: a product that is 99 percent water cannot be held to a ceiling forty times the standard its own water base must already meet. The scope note draws the boundary that makes this defensible, excluding formulated beverages from the row.

Cd.basis: as consumed, packaged aqueous beverage (read across from the Hong Kong packaged-water cell)
Cd.source_scope: Bottled or packaged drinking waters, other than natural mineral waters
Cd.label: Hong Kong Cap 132V sets cadmium in bottled or packaged drinking waters other than natural mineral waters at 3 ug/kg; it is the strictest applicable packaged-water cadmium cell and is adopted by disclosed read-across. The US 21 CFR 165.110 value (5 ug/kg) is disclosed as the looser sibling.
Cd.substantiation: Same anchor family and same reasoning as the lead cell: a flavoured water is water plus flavour, the packaged-water food law is the nearest applicable sovereign cell, and the strictest of the two applicable packaged-water values is taken. This is the only row in Category 5 that carries a numeric cadmium ceiling; every other row is a cadmium control, because no sovereign writes cadmium cells for juices, plant drinks, soft drinks, tea, coffee or infusions.

tAs.basis: as consumed, packaged aqueous beverage, total arsenic (read across from the US bottled-water standard)
tAs.label: US 21 CFR 165.110 sets arsenic in bottled water at 10 ug/kg without speciation, and Hong Kong Cap 132V sets total arsenic in packaged drinking water at the same 10 ug/kg. Two credible sovereigns converge; the value is adopted by disclosed read-across as a TOTAL-arsenic ceiling.
tAs.substantiation: This is the one place in the category where a sovereign writes an unspeciated arsenic limit for a beverage, and it is taken as written: a total, not a species. Because the total is capped at 10 ug/kg, the inorganic fraction is bounded by it (iAs <= tAs), which is why the inorganic-arsenic cell in this row is a control rather than a separate looser number. Public-water-system MCLs (US EPA and Health Canada, both 10 ug/L) are not used as anchors here for the reason given in the scope note, though they carry the same value.

iAs.rationale: No credible sovereign writes an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for a packaged water or a flavoured water; the packaged-water instruments cap arsenic as an unspeciated total, and this row adopts that total at 10 ug/kg. Publishing a separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling would either duplicate the total (adding nothing) or exceed it (an impossibility, since iAs <= tAs by identity), so the honest disposition is a control bounded by the total-arsenic ceiling rather than an invented species number. This is a control and not a not-material determination because inorganic arsenic is the health-relevant species in an aqueous matrix and is genuinely present in groundwater-sourced water: the analyte is real, only the separate ceiling is unavailable.
iAs.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by HPLC-ICP-MS, reflexed on every lot whose total arsenic exceeds 5 ug/kg (50 percent of the total-arsenic ceiling), and on every source-water change. A confirmed inorganic-arsenic result above 5 ug/kg escalates to a source-water and treatment investigation. Inorganic arsenic never substitutes for the total-arsenic report.

tHg.basis: as consumed, packaged aqueous beverage, total mercury (read across from the US bottled-water standard)
tHg.label: US 21 CFR 165.110 sets mercury in bottled water at 2 ug/kg without speciation, adopted by disclosed read-across as a total-mercury ceiling. The Hong Kong packaged-water mercury cell is written for inorganic mercury (6 ug/kg) and is therefore not a total-mercury anchor; it is disclosed but not used.
tHg.substantiation: Same anchor family as the lead, cadmium and arsenic cells in this row. Health Canada's drinking-water MCL for total mercury (1 ug/L) is stricter and is deliberately not adopted: it is a public-water-system instrument, not a packaged-food maximum level, for the reason set out in the scope note. Adopting 2 ug/kg gives this row the only numeric total-mercury ceiling in Category 5.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a packaged flavoured water: there is no marine bioaccumulation step in the supply chain and no anaerobic, sulfate-reducing methylation environment in the product or its process. Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) and is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury cell; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg). Methylmercury speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS or GC-ICP-MS) is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine lot test for this form.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish, seafood and other marine matrices (EU 2023/915 section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, Hong Kong Cap 132V fish entries). Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), which this row controls directly.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a methylmercury limit for this product form.

Ni.basis: as consumed, packaged aqueous beverage (read across from the Hong Kong packaged-water cell)
Ni.source_scope: Bottled or packaged drinking waters, other than natural mineral waters
Ni.label: Hong Kong Cap 132V sets nickel in bottled or packaged drinking waters other than natural mineral waters at 70 ug/kg; it is the strictest applicable packaged-water nickel cell and is adopted by disclosed read-across. The US 21 CFR 165.110 value (100 ug/kg) and the EU 2024/1987 beverage cell for juices and nectars (250 ug/kg) are both disclosed as looser and not adopted.
Ni.substantiation: Same anchor family and same strictest-applicable logic as the other cells in this row. Nickel in a packaged water is a source-water and stainless-plant signal; it is a Tier-2 analyte.

Sn.basis: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink liquid (inorganic tin)
Sn.label: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.5.2 sets inorganic tin in canned beverages, including canned fruit and vegetable juices, at 100 mg/kg = 100000 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V sets canned beverages at 150000 ug/kg. The EU value is the strictest applicable and binds. This is a direct sovereign maximum level on the beverage-in-a-can form, not a read-across.
Sn.substantiation: Tin in a beverage is a tinplate and can-lining migration pathway, so the government instruments are written on the canned form and the canned form is where the hazard sits. The EU cell (100000 ug/kg) directly governs every canned or tinplate-packaged product in this row and is adopted as the row ceiling for all packaging formats; a carton, PET, glass or pouch format has no tin source and complies trivially, so no separate non-canned cell is published. The looser Hong Kong canned-beverage cell (150000) and the canned-foods cells for solid foods (EU 200000; Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong 250000) are disclosed and deliberately not adopted: EU writes a stricter cell specifically for beverages and HMTc preserves that product-form split. Tin is a Tier-2 analyte; an elevated result in a non-canned format is a packaging-integrity signal.

Al.basis: as consumed, packaged aqueous beverage (read across from the US bottled-water secondary level)
Al.label: US 21 CFR 165.110 sets a secondary allowable level for aluminium in bottled water of 200 ug/kg, adopted by disclosed read-across. This is the only numeric aluminium ceiling in Category 5; every other row is an aluminium control because no credible sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for a formulated beverage or a dry beverage commodity.
Al.substantiation: The value is a secondary (aesthetic) allowable level rather than a health-based maximum, and that is stated plainly rather than dressed up: HMTc adopts it because it is a real sovereign number written for exactly this aqueous packaged form, and because a published ceiling with a disclosed regulatory character is more defensible than a control on a cell where a sovereign number exists. Mineral water is exempt from the aesthetic levels in the instrument and routes to Category 8 in any case. The EU 2020/2184 drinking-water value (200 ug/L) and Health Canada's operational guidance (2900 ug/L) are public-supply instruments and are not used as anchors.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is recorded as a SCREEN, not as a protective standalone ceiling: the sovereign packaged-water chromium values are written for total chromium, which in an aqueous matrix is dominated by benign Cr(III), while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI). The number is published because a sovereign wrote it for this exact form; the Cr-VI cell in this row carries the species control.
Cr.basis: as consumed, packaged aqueous beverage, total chromium (read across from the Hong Kong packaged-water cell)
Cr.source_scope: Bottled or packaged drinking waters, other than natural mineral waters
Cr.label: Hong Kong Cap 132V sets total chromium in bottled or packaged drinking waters other than natural mineral waters at 50 ug/kg; it is the strictest applicable packaged-water total-chromium cell and is adopted by disclosed read-across. The US 21 CFR 165.110 value (100 ug/kg) is disclosed as looser.
Cr.substantiation: Same anchor family as the rest of this row. Recorded as a screen rather than a firm limit because a total-element value cannot by itself be protective against the toxic species; the species obligation sits in the Cr-VI control, which for this near-neutral aqueous matrix is a control and not a not-material determination.

Cr-VI.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for any food or beverage, and the in-matrix reduction argument that supports a not-material determination in an acidic beverage is not available here: a flavoured water is near-neutral (typically pH 5.5 to 7.5) and carries almost none of the organic acid, sugar or ascorbate load that reduces Cr(VI) to Cr(III) in a juice or soft drink, and hexavalent chromium is known to persist in oxygenated aqueous matrices, which is precisely why water law regulates chromium at all. Because Cr(VI) cannot be assumed to be reduced to Cr(III) in this matrix, the fail-safe disposition is a control rather than a not-material determination, and no ceiling is invented.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Cr(VI)-specific speciation (IC-ICP-MS, EN 15192 adapted) is reflexed whenever total chromium exceeds 100 ug/kg in this form, or 50 percent of the total-chromium screen value where this row publishes one. A confirmed Cr(VI) detection escalates to a process-water, equipment and ingredient investigation and blocks certification pending resolution.
